items.informal_name: Evaluation of Bivariate Polynomial at X Recovers Original Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : Polynomial (Polynomial R)},
  Polynomial.eval (Polynomial.C Polynomial.X)
      (Polynomial.eval₂ (Polynomial.mapRingHom (algebraMap R (Polynomial (Polynomial R)))) (Polynomial.C Polynomial.X)
        p) =
    p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ in $ R[X][Y] $, evaluating $ p $ at $ Y = X $ (considered as a constant polynomial in $ R[X] $) results in $ p $ itself. This identity demonstrates that substituting the variable $ Y $ with the indeterminate $ X $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X][Y] $ preserves the original polynomial.

items.informal_name: Evaluation After Substitution Equals Evaluation at Substituted Value
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → R) (i : σ) (p : Polynomial R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval f) ((Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i) p) = Polynomial.eval (f i) p
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to R $, any $ i \in \sigma $, and any polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, the evaluation of the multivariate polynomial obtained by substituting the variable $ X $ with $ X_i $ in $ p $, using $ f $, equals the evaluation of $ p $ at $ f(i) $. Formally, $ \text{eval}(f, p.\text{toMvPolynomial}(i)) = \text{eval}(f(i), p) $.

items.informal_name: Eval₂ Coincides with Ring Homomorphism on Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {S : Type v} [inst : CommRing S] {R : Type u} (c : ℤ →+* S) (f : MvPolynomial R ℤ →+* S) (x : MvPolynomial R ℤ),
  MvPolynomial.eval₂ c (⇑f ∘ MvPolynomial.X) x = f x
items.informal_description: For any ring homomorphism $ f : R[\sigma] \to S $, coefficient map $ c : \mathbb{Z} \to S $, and polynomial $ x \in R[\sigma] $, evaluating $ x $ using the `eval₂` function with coefficient map $ c $ and variable map $ f \circ X $ yields the same result as applying $ f $ directly to $ x $, i.e., $ \text{eval}_2(c, f \circ X, x) = f(x) $.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Compatibility with Fin(n+1) to Fin(n) Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → R} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R)
  (q : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval x) (Polynomial.eval q ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f)) =
    (MvPolynomial.eval fun i => Fin.cases ((MvPolynomial.eval x) q) x i) f
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, natural number $ n $, evaluation map $ x : \text{Fin}(n) \to R $, multivariate polynomial $ f \in R[\text{Fin}(n+1)] $, and coefficient polynomial $ q \in R[\text{Fin}(n)] $, evaluating $ f $ after applying the $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $-to-\text{Fin}(n) algebra equivalence with outer variable substitution $ q $ is equivalent to directly evaluating $ f $ with the first variable replaced by $ q $ and other variables evaluated via $ x $. This establishes consistency between nested polynomial evaluations and direct evaluation under variable renaming.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials over Fin(n+1) and Univariate Polynomials with Coefficients in Fin(n) Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → R) (y : R) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval (Fin.cons y s)) f =
    Polynomial.eval y (Polynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval s) ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f))
items.informal_description: Evaluating a multivariate polynomial $ f $ in $ n+1 $ variables at a tuple $ (y, s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_n) $ is equivalent to first applying the $ \text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n)) $ variable equivalence to express $ f $ as a univariate polynomial in $ y $ with coefficients in $ n $-variable polynomials, then evaluating this outer polynomial at $ y $ after evaluating its coefficients using $ s $.
